~ NPC dialogue line
~ Hm.  That's a really big ask.  You seem to be the sort of person who
would ask for this kind of thing, but are you certain you want to be
permanently attached to this suitcase?  You sure you're thinking clearly?
This isn't like the CBMs I sell.  There's no going back.  And you better be
able to produce enough power.  These need constant power.  Without it,
you're as good as dead.  For a Cyberframe like mine, one power storage unit
will last less than an hour of walking.  Less if you're fighting or
running.  It's not an easy life.
identity: Hm.  A mighty ask on a mighty ask.  Ye certainly got the disposition, but you sure you wanna be cut inta' this crowded space?"  Rubik taps their metal torso.  "You sure ya' lump is screwed on tight?  This isn't like the bright'n'steelies on offer.  No goin' back.  And ye best be happy with the amount'a power you can generate.  This'ere needs contant power.  Without power, yer good as dead.  The power storage units?  Fer a case this'n kind, one'a the power storage units buys you a little-less'an an hour of walkin'.  Less for scrappin' and scramblin'.  Nothin's easy about it."

entries.developer_comments:
~ Snippet in category 'lab_file_photokinesis'
~ Phavian designation for photokinetic study is CRYPTIC FORGE
identity:
How does CRYPTIC FORGE control darkness?  Darkness is not a thing, there are no "skotons" that they could emit to cancel out existing light, but that seems to the casual observer what is happening.

B81 was instructed to cancel the light within a one-meter area in the center of the testing chamber.  The lights were extinguished and blackout curtains hung over all observation windows.  The area was first exposed to candlelight (12 lumens), showing a distinct border of the area.  A flashlight (350 lumens) was trained on the area as well, with a similar effect, though the directional light from the flashlight was sufficient to demonstrate that light did not penetrate the area.  A high-powered flashlight (6000 lumens) shown from the corner illuminated most of the testing area and clearly delineated the borders of the area, as well as casting a shadow on the wall opposite of the light source.  Finally, the blackout curtains were removed and, after instructing B81 to close their eyes, a floodlight (118K lumens) was shone on the area, again to no effect.

The initial hypothesis, that CRYPTIC FORGE is somehow suppressing or allowing photons to "jump" through the area, is incorrect.  Assuming that conservation of energy is still in effect (since, without assuming that we have no basis to determine anything), it is instead possible that the photons are somehow absorbed by the affected area in a way that does not inhibit movement, in the same way that space seems mostly empty but large amounts of radiation are absorbed by cosmic dust.  Unfortunate that we don't have access to a particle accelerator to test various particles' interactions with the effect.

I have already submitted a proposal to test CRYPTIC FORGE's ability to block microwaves, radio waves, X-rays, and other elements of the electromagnetic spectrum, and am waiting on successful procurement of the necessary equipment.
Adam Brenner
Researcher
